# Prover SDK API reference

API version **1** (`AEGIS_SDK_API_VERSION`). Generated from [`sdk/include/aegis_sdk.h`](../sdk/include/aegis_sdk.h), the one public header, in its order and with its own words; the header is authoritative. The integrator's guide is [`docs/sdk-porting-guide.md`](sdk-porting-guide.md), what may change between versions is in [`docs/sdk-versioning.md`](sdk-versioning.md).

## Overview

Aegis Prover SDK: the public interface of the protocol core (sdk/src/aegis_proto.c) and of the platform layer a device maker writes for it. sdk/README.md is the integrator's guide; this file is the reference.

The core is the device's side of the Aegis attestation protocol: an ML-DSA-65 quote, an ML-KEM-768 session bound to that quote by one signed transcript, a credential from the verifier, KMAC256 heartbeats, and the session's end on the device's own clock. It is plain C11 (<stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, and memcpy, memset, memcmp, strlen and strcmp of <string.h>), allocates nothing, and keeps all its state in a context and one work buffer that the caller provides. It reaches the device through the functions of struct aegis_platform, and the network not at all: the integrator carries messages to and from it, either as text lines (aegis_prover_handle_line) or as binary operations (aegis_prover_*).

Everything declared here runs in the device's secure world (a TF-M secure partition, a trusted application, or the whole firmware on a chip without one): the context holds the secret keys.

Memory, a security requirement of every function below: whatever the caller passes in (a line, a challenge, a nonce, a ciphertext, a credential, a status text) must lie in memory that the caller owns alone for the duration of the call. Nothing less trusted may be able to write it meanwhile: not the non-secure side through a mapped message buffer or shared memory, not a peripheral through DMA. A transport that receives requests in such memory copies them into the secure world first (every port here does). The binary operations take their inputs once and work on their own copies from then on, so that what is accepted is what was checked; the line transport parses the line where it stands and has no such second line of defence.

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_PK_LEN` | `1952u` | ML-DSA-65 public key (FIPS 204) |
| `AEGIS_SK_LEN` | `4032u` | ML-DSA-65 secret key |
| `AEGIS_SIG_LEN` | `3309u` | ML-DSA-65 signature |
| `AEGIS_SEED_LEN` | `32u` | ML-DSA-65 key generation seed; also the length of the exchange root |
| `AEGIS_KEM_EK_LEN` | `1184u` | ML-KEM-768 encapsulation key (FIPS 203) |
| `AEGIS_KEM_DK_LEN` | `2400u` | ML-KEM-768 decapsulation key |
| `AEGIS_KEM_CT_LEN` | `1088u` | ML-KEM-768 ciphertext |
| `AEGIS_CHALLENGE_LEN` | `32u` | the verifier's challenge, and its nonces |
| `AEGIS_DIGEST_LEN` | `32u` |  |
| `AEGIS_TAG_LEN` | `32u` | the confirmation tag of a finished exchange |
| `AEGIS_HB_LEN` | `40u` | a heartbeat: counter (8 bytes, little-endian) \|\| KMAC256 tag (32) |
| `AEGIS_SESSION_LEN` | `64u` | session id (32) \|\| SHA3-256 of the credential (32) |

A credential is "<canonical JSON body>\n<ML-DSA-65 signature>"; longer ones are refused.

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_CRED_MAX` | `6144u` |  |
| `AEGIS_CRED_BODY_MAX` | `(AEGIS_CRED_MAX - 1u - AEGIS_SIG_LEN)` |  |

The work buffer (struct aegis_config). The core builds in it whatever is signed or verified: a label, a zero byte and the message. Its size sets two limits:

     evidence (the claims, or the platform's token)   work_len - AEGIS_WORK_QUOTE_HEAD bytes
     credential body                                  work_len - AEGIS_WORK_CRED_HEAD bytes

and it is never less than AEGIS_WORK_MIN, the message under a KEM key's signature. AEGIS_WORK_LEN() gives the size for a wanted evidence limit; with it every credential the protocol allows fits. A port that must save RAM can give AEGIS_WORK_MIN: credentials are then limited to bodies of 1214 bytes (the gateway's are about 600).

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_WORK_QUOTE_HEAD` | `24u` | "aegis-endpoint-quote-v1" and its terminator |
| `AEGIS_WORK_CRED_HEAD` | `20u` | "aegis-credential-v1" and its terminator |
| `AEGIS_WORK_MIN` | `(18u + AEGIS_CHALLENGE_LEN + AEGIS_KEM_EK_LEN)` |  |
| `AEGIS_WORK_CRED` | `(AEGIS_WORK_CRED_HEAD + AEGIS_CRED_BODY_MAX)` |  |
| `AEGIS_WORK_LEN(evidence_max)` | `(AEGIS_WORK_QUOTE_HEAD + (evidence_max) > AEGIS_WORK_CRED ? AEGIS_WORK_QUOTE_HEAD + (evidence_max) : AEGIS_WORK_CRED)` |  |

The line transport (aegis_prover_handle_line). The longest request is PQKEMFIN: a ciphertext and a credential in hex. The longest reply is PQTOKEN: evidence and a signature in hex. AEGIS_REPLY_MAX fits evidence of up to 1440 bytes; AEGIS_REPLY_LEN() gives the size for another limit.

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_LINE_MAX` | `14600u` |  |
| `AEGIS_REPLY_LEN(evidence_max)` | `(2u * ((evidence_max) + AEGIS_SIG_LEN) + 64u)` |  |
| `AEGIS_REPLY_MAX` | `9600u` |  |
| `AEGIS_STATUS_MAX` | `96u` | the platform's heartbeat status text in the line transport, with its terminator |

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_HB_TTL_MAX` | `15u` | ";ttl=<seconds>" as the core appends it to a heartbeat's status: at most this many bytes |

A session ends on the device's own clock (docs/endpoint-expiry.md). The credential's lifetime is its signed "expires" minus "issued", at most AEGIS_CRED_LIFETIME_MAX seconds; the session lives that long plus a margin of one sixteenth. The margin covers a clock up to 6 % fast (the least exact one in use is the STM32's RC oscillator, good to a few per cent), so a device does not end a session before the verifier's own expiry.

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_CRED_LIFETIME_MAX` | `86400u` |  |
| `AEGIS_SESSION_LIMIT(lifetime)` | `((uint64_t)(lifetime) + (lifetime) / 16u)` |  |

## Results

### `enum aegis_result`

What an operation returns. The line transport turns each into the reply given on the right; a binary transport maps them to its own codes (endpoints/stm32h573/tfm-aegis-partition/aegis_pq_attest.c maps them to PSA statuses). Any result but AEGIS_OK means that nothing was written to the operation's outputs.

| Value | Name | Meaning |

| 0 | `AEGIS_OK` |  |
| 1 | `AEGIS_ERR_ARGUMENT` | a NULL or out-of-range argument of the caller's: a programming error |
| 2 | `AEGIS_ERR_VERSION` | aegis_prover_init: built against another API version or layout |
| 3 | `AEGIS_ERR_IDENTITY` | aegis_prover_init: no identity key (key generation or the platform failed, or the seed or the exchange root is all zero) |
| 4 | `AEGIS_ERR_BAD_REQUEST` | "ERR bad-request" a length the protocol does not allow |
| 5 | `AEGIS_ERR_EVIDENCE` | "ERR evidence" the platform gave no evidence, or it does not fit |
| 6 | `AEGIS_ERR_RNG` | "ERR rng" no fresh randomness for the exchange's key: the generator failed, or gave 32 equal bytes or its last output again |
| 7 | `AEGIS_ERR_SIGN_RNG` | "ERR sign" no fresh randomness for a signature |
| 8 | `AEGIS_ERR_SIGN` | "ERR sign" the signature could not be made |
| 9 | `AEGIS_ERR_KEM` | "ERR kem" ML-KEM key generation or decapsulation failed |
| 10 | `AEGIS_ERR_NO_EXCHANGE` | "ERR cred no-exchange" no exchange is pending |
| 11 | `AEGIS_ERR_CLOCK` | "ERR clock" the clock cannot be trusted: no session starts |
| 12 | `AEGIS_ERR_CRED_SIGNATURE` | "ERR cred signature" not signed by the pinned verifier key |

## The platform layer

### `struct aegis_measurement`

One measured software component (PSA claim names): its type label, its SHA-256 (or other 32-byte) digest and a description for the verifier's journal. The verifier's policy compares label and value with reference values.

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `const char *label` | for example "SPE", "NSPE", "APP"; must stay valid while the list is in use |
| `uint8_t value[AEGIS_DIGEST_LEN]` |  |
| `char desc[64]` | a terminated text |

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_COMPAT_HB_COUNTER_FROM_BOOT` | `0x01u` | Compatibility with images in the field. A new port sets none of them. The heartbeat counter counts from the start of the device, not from the start of each session (the STM32H573 partition up to SPE 3183f74a). The verifier only needs it to rise within a session. |

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_COMPAT_CRED_WITHOUT_ENDPOINT` | `0x02u` | A credential need not name this device's key in "endpoint_pq_pk_sha256" (the same partition). It must still name this exchange's ML-KEM key, which no other device has. |

### `struct aegis_platform`

What the device gives the core. Every function gets `user` back as its first argument and returns 0 for success; any other value makes the core refuse the request that needed it (it never continues with a default). The core keeps a pointer to the structure, not a copy: it must stay valid and unchanged for as long as the context is used, in memory only the secure world can write. Make it const (ROM): whoever can change a function pointer in it runs code in the secure world. A function may take as long as it needs; the core itself never waits for anything.

Required: random, clock and clock_hz, and one of measurements and evidence.

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `void *user` |  |
| `int (*random)(void *user, uint8_t *out, size_t n)` | Randomness. n bytes (32 at a time) from the chip's random number generator or a DRBG seeded from it. They go into every exchange's ML-KEM key and, hedged, into every signature. A failure refuses the request. For an exchange's key the core also refuses 32 equal bytes (a generator that reports success and writes nothing, or one constant) and the bytes of the draw before (a generator that stands still). These are the failures it can see, not a health test: the quality of the bytes is the platform's. In particular the generator must not restart with the same output after a reset, which the core cannot notice: the exchange keys then repeat, and a recorded exchange can be replayed (tests/host/test_reset_replay_check.py shows it). |
| `int (*clock)(void *user, uint64_t *now)` | Time. A counter that only advances, at clock_hz counts a second (1 or more), from any origin, and that nothing outside the secure world can set, slow or stop. It is read at every request. A failure, or a reading below the one at a session's start, ends the session and lets none start: return nonzero whenever the counter can no longer be trusted (a changed clock source, a wrap that may have been missed). |
| `uint32_t clock_hz` |  |
| `int (*measurements)(void *user, const struct aegis_measurement **list, size_t *count)` | Evidence, variant 1: the measurements, as taken by code the measured code cannot change (the boot stage before it, or the secure world before the non-secure image runs). *list points to *count entries that stay valid until the next call. The core puts them into the Aegis claims (CBOR, PSA claim numbers) with `profile` and `version` and signs them; an entry without a label, or claims that do not fit the work buffer, refuse the quote. Leave NULL when `evidence` is set. |
| `const char *profile` | the claims' profile name: tells the verifier what kind of device and key this is |
| `const char *version` | the measured components' version text |
| `int (*evidence)(void *user, const uint8_t challenge[AEGIS_CHALLENGE_LEN], uint8_t *out, size_t cap, size_t *len)` | Evidence, variant 2 (instead of 1): the platform's own token for this challenge, at most cap bytes, its length in *len (for example TF-M's PSA initial attestation token, which carries the boot measurements under the platform's key). The core signs it as it is; a length of 0 or beyond cap refuses the quote. This is also where an EAT / COSE encoder goes. |
| `int (*identity_public_key)(void *user, uint8_t pk[AEGIS_PK_LEN])` | Identity key held by the platform (a secure element, a key store, an accelerator). Set both or neither. With both set the core never sees the secret key: struct aegis_config.identity_seed is then NULL. identity_sign signs msg with pure ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204 ML-DSA.Sign, empty context string), hedged. |
| `int (*identity_sign)(void *user, const uint8_t *msg, size_t msg_len, uint8_t sig[AEGIS_SIG_LEN])` |  |
| `int (*status)(void *user, char *buf, size_t cap)` | Optional, for the line transport's PQHB: the device's status text (key=value;key=value, printable, no "ttl=" key) into buf, terminated; returns its length, or a negative value. It must be shorter than cap. The verifier shows the text and can match it; it is under the heartbeat's MAC. Without it the status is empty. |
| `uint32_t compat` | AEGIS_COMPAT_*, normally 0 |

## The context

### `struct aegis_prover`

The prover's whole state. The caller provides the storage (static, in secure RAM that does not keep its content across a reset) and never reads or writes a member: the layout is here only so that its size is known. Nothing in it is persistent and nothing may be made so: a session and the quote an exchange continues must not outlive a reset.

| Member | Meaning |

| `uint8_t quote_ch[AEGIS_CHALLENGE_LEN], quote_t1[AEGIS_DIGEST_LEN]` | the last quote signed since the start |

### `struct aegis_config`

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `const struct aegis_platform *platform` |  |
| `const uint8_t *verifier_pk` | The verifier's (gateway's) ML-DSA-65 public key, AEGIS_PK_LEN bytes, pinned in the image. Not copied: the core keeps the pointer, so the key must stay valid and unchanged in memory only the secure world can write (const, in ROM, part of the measured image). Only credentials signed with it start a session. |
| `const uint8_t *identity_seed` | The identity key's seed, AEGIS_SEED_LEN bytes, device-unique and derived from a hardware secret that only the secure world can use. The core makes the ML-DSA-65 key pair from it (the same pair at every start) and does not keep it: wipe your copy when aegis_prover_init() returns. NULL when the platform holds the key. A seed of 32 zero bytes is refused (as is such an exchange root): it is what a derivation that failed leaves. |
| `const uint8_t *exchange_root` | A second device-unique secret, AEGIS_SEED_LEN bytes, used only in the derivation of the exchanges' ML-KEM keys (with fresh randomness, the nonce and a counter). Copied into the context; wipe your copy. |
| `uint8_t *work` | The work buffer: at least AEGIS_WORK_MIN bytes, see AEGIS_WORK_LEN(). Used only by the core, from its first operation on: aegis_prover_init() reads the seed and the root before anything is written to it, so a port short of stack may derive both in the work buffer and wipe them there afterwards (the STM32 port does). |
| `size_t work_len` |  |

## The core

One context serves one request at a time (no locking inside). Every function below except aegis_prover_init and aegis_prover_public_key first reads the clock and ends a session that has outlived its credential. Output pointers (*evidence, *sig, *ek) point into the context or the work buffer and are valid until the next call with the same context.

### `aegis_prover_init()`

```c
int aegis_prover_init(struct aegis_prover *p, size_t prover_size, uint32_t api_version, const struct aegis_config *cfg);
```

At every start of the device, before the first request: checks the configuration, wipes the context, makes or fetches the identity key. prover_size and api_version are the caller's sizeof(struct aegis_prover) and AEGIS_SDK_API_VERSION: use AEGIS_PROVER_INIT(). Until it has returned AEGIS_OK every other function refuses.

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_PROVER_INIT(p, cfg)` | `aegis_prover_init((p), sizeof(struct aegis_prover), AEGIS_SDK_API_VERSION, (cfg))` |  |

### `aegis_prover_public_key()`

```c
const uint8_t *aegis_prover_public_key(const struct aegis_prover *p);
```

The identity public key (AEGIS_PK_LEN bytes), or NULL before a successful init.

### `aegis_prover_poll()`

```c
void aegis_prover_poll(struct aegis_prover *p);
```

Read the clock and end an overdue session, nothing else. A transport may call it for requests it refuses itself, and a device may call it from a timer, so that the session key is wiped when the session ends and not only at the next request.

### `aegis_prover_quote()`

```c
int aegis_prover_quote(struct aegis_prover *p, const uint8_t challenge[AEGIS_CHALLENGE_LEN], const uint8_t **evidence, size_t *evidence_len, const uint8_t **sig);
```

Quote: evidence for this challenge and its ML-DSA-65 signature over "aegis-endpoint-quote-v1\0" || evidence. It becomes the one quote an exchange can continue, in place of any earlier one.

### `aegis_prover_kem_init()`

```c
int aegis_prover_kem_init(struct aegis_prover *p, const uint8_t nonce[AEGIS_CHALLENGE_LEN], const uint8_t **ek, const uint8_t **sig);
```

Start an exchange: a fresh ML-KEM-768 key and the identity key's signature for it. A nonce equal to the challenge of the last quote continues that quote (once): the signature is then over the transcript. Replaces a pending exchange; an established session stays until an exchange completes.

### `aegis_prover_kem_pending()`

```c
int aegis_prover_kem_pending(struct aegis_prover *p);
```

May an exchange be finished now? AEGIS_OK, AEGIS_ERR_NO_EXCHANGE or AEGIS_ERR_CLOCK: what aegis_prover_kem_finish would answer first. For a transport that wants to refuse before it reads a large message.

### `aegis_prover_kem_finish()`

```c
int aegis_prover_kem_finish(struct aegis_prover *p, const uint8_t ct[AEGIS_KEM_CT_LEN], const uint8_t *cred, size_t cred_len, uint8_t tag[AEGIS_TAG_LEN]);
```

Finish the exchange: check the verifier's credential (cred_len bytes, 1 to AEGIS_CRED_MAX), decapsulate, start the session, give the confirmation tag. ct and cred are only read. A refused credential ends the exchange and leaves an established session alone; AEGIS_ERR_NO_EXCHANGE, AEGIS_ERR_CLOCK and AEGIS_ERR_BAD_REQUEST leave both.

### `aegis_prover_session_state()`

```c
int aegis_prover_session_state(struct aegis_prover *p, uint32_t *ttl_s);
```

Is there a session? AEGIS_OK (and, if ttl_s is not NULL, the seconds it has left, rounded up), AEGIS_ERR_NO_SESSION or AEGIS_ERR_EXPIRED.

### `aegis_prover_session()`

```c
int aegis_prover_session(struct aegis_prover *p, uint8_t out[AEGIS_SESSION_LEN]);
```

The session's public name: SHA3-256("aegis-session-id-v1" || session key) || SHA3-256(credential).

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_HB_RAW` | `0x01u` | Heartbeat: a counter and KMAC256(session key, nonce \|\| counter \|\| status, 256, "aegis-hb-v2"). status holds *status_len bytes of the device's status text in a buffer of status_cap bytes. The core appends ";ttl=<seconds the session has left>" (up to AEGIS_HB_TTL_MAX bytes; AEGIS_ERR_BUFFER if they do not fit), updates *status_len, and the MAC covers the whole text: send it with the heartbeat. The text before it must not hold a "ttl=" key that an untrusted party chose. With AEGIS_HB_RAW the status is MACed as given, for a transport with no way to return it (the verifier then does not learn the time left). |

### `aegis_prover_heartbeat()`

```c
int aegis_prover_heartbeat(struct aegis_prover *p, const uint8_t nonce[AEGIS_CHALLENGE_LEN], char *status, size_t *status_len, size_t status_cap, uint32_t flags, uint8_t out[AEGIS_HB_LEN]);
```

### `aegis_prover_handle_line()`

```c
int aegis_prover_handle_line(struct aegis_prover *p, char *line, char *out, size_t cap);
```

The line transport: one request line (terminated text, changed in place) in, one reply (terminated, without a line end) out; returns the reply's length, or -1 if cap cannot hold any reply (give AEGIS_REPLY_MAX).

     PQKEY                    -> PQKEY <len> <hex> END
     PQCHAL <challenge>       -> PQTOKEN <len> <evidence> <len> <sig> END
     PQKEMINIT <nonce>        -> PQKEMEK <len> <ek> <len> <sig> END
     PQKEMFIN <ct> <cred>     -> PQKEMOK <tag> END
     PQHB <nonce>             -> PQHB <status> <counter> <tag> END
     PQSESSION                -> PQSESSION <session id> <credential hash> END
     PQEAT <challenge>        -> PQEAT <len> <COSE_Sign1> END          (only with -DAEGIS_EAT_COSE=1, below)

and "ERR <reason>" (enum aegis_result; also "ERR empty", "ERR unknown"). Binary fields are in hex. A transport that reads a line longer than AEGIS_LINE_MAX answers "ERR too-long" itself.

## Standard evidence (an option)

Built only with -DAEGIS_EAT_COSE=1, for the core and for whoever includes this file; off by default, and a build without it is unchanged. docs/evidence-format.md is the specification.

The same quote as an EAT (RFC 9711) in a COSE_Sign1 (RFC 9052) signed with ML-DSA-65 (RFC 9964, algorithm -49) by the identity key: a verifier, or anyone with a COSE library and the device's public key, reads it without Aegis code. The claims are the challenge (eat_nonce), the UEID (0x01 || SHA-256 of the identity key), the profile, and either the platform's measurements as measured components (RFC 10013: label, the platform's version text and the SHA-256 digest; the description is not carried) with the platform's profile name, or the platform's own token (struct aegis_platform.evidence) nested as the submodule "platform". At most 16 measurements; a label is 1 to 64 bytes of text, the version at most 64.

It is a quote like the other: it becomes the one quote an exchange can continue, in place of any earlier one of either kind. The transcript then hashes the COSE Sig_structure, the bytes this signature covers.

Memory: the work buffer must hold AEGIS_EAT_WORK_MIN bytes (AEGIS_WORK_LEN() always gives more) and AEGIS_EAT_PAYLOAD_AT more than the claims; a platform token may be as long as the work buffer less 230 bytes. The whole object is AEGIS_EAT_LEN(claims) bytes at most: about 3.6 kB with two measurements.

| Macro | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS_EAT_WORK_MIN` *(only with `-DAEGIS_EAT_COSE=1`)* | `(10u + AEGIS_PK_LEN)` | the identity key as a COSE_Key, hashed for the key identifier |
| `AEGIS_EAT_PAYLOAD_AT` *(only with `-DAEGIS_EAT_COSE=1`)* | `78u` | the COSE Sig_structure's bytes before the claims, at their most |
| `AEGIS_EAT_LEN(claims)` *(only with `-DAEGIS_EAT_COSE=1`)* | `((claims) + AEGIS_EAT_PAYLOAD_AT + 6u + AEGIS_SIG_LEN - 13u)` |  |

### `aegis_prover_quote_eat()` *(only with `-DAEGIS_EAT_COSE=1`)*

```c
int aegis_prover_quote_eat(struct aegis_prover *p, const uint8_t challenge[AEGIS_CHALLENGE_LEN], uint8_t *out, size_t cap, size_t *len);
```

The EAT for this challenge into out (cap bytes), its length in *len. AEGIS_ERR_BUFFER if cap is less than AEGIS_EAT_LEN(0); AEGIS_ERR_EVIDENCE if the platform gives no evidence, or the claims do not fit cap or the work buffer (a platform's token gets exactly the room that is left, as for aegis_prover_quote); the errors of aegis_prover_quote otherwise. The line transport: PQEAT <challenge> -> PQEAT <len> <hex> END.

### `aegis_wipe()`

```c
void aegis_wipe(void *p, size_t n);
```

Overwrite n bytes with zeros in a way the compiler does not remove: for a port's copies of seeds and keys.
